mishnayos.summary: What happens if the beis din made a mistake and ruled that something forbidden is allowed, and a person followed them? If he relied on the beis din he does not bring a korban, but if he knew better, he does.

chunks.en: If the beis din ruled that people may break
chunks.st: If a court erroneously issued a ruling permitting the Jewish people to violate

chunks.st: one of all the mitzvot that are stated in the Torah,

chunks.en: and one person went and did it by mistake because of what they said,
chunks.st: and an individual proceeded and performed that transgression unwittingly on the basis of the court’s ruling,

words.note: Following their ruling.

chunks.en: whether they did it and he did it with them,
chunks.st: then whether the judges performed the transgression and he performed it with them,

chunks.en: or they did it and he did it after them,

chunks.en: or they did not do it but he did,
chunks.st: or whether the judges did not perform the transgression and he performed it alone,

chunks.en: he is free from bringing a korban, because he relied on the beis din.
chunks.st: in all these cases the individual is exempt from bringing an offering. This is due to the fact that he associated his action with the ruling of the court.

words.note: He does not have to bring a korban.

mishnayos.summary: The beis din brings a korban for a mistaken ruling only if they changed a part of a mitzvah. If they said a whole mitzvah is not in the Torah at all, they do not bring a korban.

chunks.en: If the beis din ruled to uproot
a whole mitzvah,

words.note: The whole mitzvah, not just one detail.

chunks.en: and they said, "There is no law of niddah in the Torah,"

words.note: Laws of a kind of tumah of a married woman.

chunks.en: "There is no Shabbos in the Torah,"
"There is no avodah zarah in the Torah,"

words.note: Avodah zarah is serving idols.

chunks.en: they are free from bringing a korban.
If they ruled to cancel part of a mitzvah and keep part of it,
they must bring a korban.
How is that? They said,
"There is a law of niddah in the Torah,
but in the case of a woman who waits

words.note: A woman who must wait a clean day before she is tahor again.

chunks.en: one clean day for one day, one is free."
"There is Shabbos in the Torah,

chunks.he: אֲבָל הַמּוֹצִיא מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
chunks.en: but one who carries something out from a private place to a public place
is free." "There is avodah zarah in the Torah,
but one who only bows down to it is free."
These must bring a korban,
because it says in the Torah, "And a thing is hidden,"
a thing, and not the whole mitzvah.

mishnayos.summary: The beis din brings a korban for a mistaken ruling only if all the judges were fit to rule and agreed. It also teaches who brings which korban when the judges or the people sinned by mistake or on purpose.

chunks.en: If the beis din ruled,
and one of the judges knew that they made a mistake,
and he said to them, "You are making a mistake,"
or if the greatest judge

words.note: The mufla is the head and wisest judge of the Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: of the beis din was not there,
or if one of the judges was a ger,

words.note: Someone who was not born Jewish and became Jewish.

chunks.en: or a mamzer, or a Givoni,

words.note: Someone whose family line makes him unfit to judge on the Sanhedrin.
From the Givonim, who joined the Jews in Yehoshua's time.

chunks.he: אוֹ זָקֵן שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה לוֹ בָנִים,
chunks.en: or an old man who could no longer have children,
they are free from bringing a korban,
because it says here, "assembly,"

words.note: The Torah uses this word for the beis din.

chunks.en: and it says there, "assembly."
Just as the "assembly" said there means
that all of them must be fit to give rulings,
so too the "assembly" said here means
that all of them must be fit to give rulings.
If the beis din ruled by mistake
and the whole community did it by mistake,
they bring a bull as a korban.
If they ruled on purpose, and the people did it by mistake,
chunks.explain: The judges knew the ruling was wrong.

chunks.en: each one brings a female lamb or a female goat.
If they ruled by mistake, and the people did it on purpose,
they are free from bringing a korban.

mishnayos.summary: If the Kohen Gadol made a mistake in a ruling for himself and then did the sin by mistake, he brings a bull as a korban. His ruling for himself is like the beis din's ruling for everyone.

chunks.en: If the anointed Kohen ruled for himself,
chunks.st: In a case where an anointed priest, i.e., the High Priest, issued an erroneous ruling for himself
chunks.stMore: permitting performance of an action prohibited by Torah law,

words.note: The Kohen Gadol, who was anointed with special oil.

chunks.en: by mistake, and did it by mistake,
chunks.st: if he issued the ruling unwittingly and then unwittingly performed the transgression in accordance with his ruling,

chunks.en: he brings a bull as a korban.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a bull as a sin-offering for an unwitting transgression by the anointed priest.

chunks.en: If he ruled by mistake but did it on purpose,
chunks.st: If he issued the ruling unwittingly, and performed the transgression intentionally,

chunks.en: or ruled on purpose but did it by mistake,
chunks.st: or if he issued the ruling intentionally and performed the transgression unwittingly,

chunks.en: he is free, because the ruling of the anointed Kohen for himself
chunks.st: he is exempt from liability to bring any offering, as there is a principle: The legal status of the ruling of an anointed priest for himself is like

chunks.en: is like the ruling of the beis din for the whole community.
chunks.st: that of the ruling of the court for the general public.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, the High Priest is liable to bring the bull as a sin-offering for his unwitting transgression in a case when the court would be liable to bring the bull as a communal sin-offering for an unwitting transgression performed by the general public.

mishnayos.summary: If the Kohen Gadol ruled and sinned alone, he brings his own korban; if he was part of the beis din's ruling, he is forgiven together with everyone. A korban is brought only when part of a mitzvah was changed, even for avodah zarah.

chunks.en: If he ruled together with the community and did it with the community,

mishnayos.summary: The beis din does not bring a korban for a mistaken ruling about the mitzvos of keeping the Beis HaMikdash tahor, but it does for the mitzvos of niddah.

chunks.en: They do not bring a korban for a mitzvah to do

words.note: A mitzvah that tells us to do something.

chunks.en: or a mitzvah not to do, about the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.explain: Mitzvos about not coming into the Beis HaMikdash when tamei.

chunks.en: and one does not bring an asham talui for

mishnayos.summary: The beis din does not bring a korban for a mistaken ruling about three special kinds of sins. The Rabbis argue whether the king is also free from korbanos for them.

chunks.en: They do not bring a korban for "hearing the voice,"
chunks.explain: A witness who falsely swears he knows nothing.
chunks.st: The court is not liable for issuing a ruling with regard to hearing of a voice,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a false oath of testimony taken by a witness who refuses to testify on behalf of a litigant who demands that he testify,

chunks.en: or for "saying with the lips,"
chunks.explain: A false promise made with a shevuah.
chunks.st: or for an utterance of the lips,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a false oath stated about some matter,

chunks.en: or for making the Beis HaMikdash or its korbanos tamei.
chunks.st: or for the defiling of the Temple or its sacrificial foods.

chunks.en: And the king is like them.
chunks.st: And the status of the king is like

chunks.en: the king must bring a korban for all of them, except for "hearing the voice,"
chunks.st: The king is liable in all of those cases except for the case of hearing of a voice,
chunks.stMore: and even in that case, his exemption is not intrinsic to the mitzva. Rather, it is for technical reasons,

chunks.he: שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ לֹא דָן וְלֹא דָנִין אוֹתוֹ,
chunks.en: because the king does not judge, and others do not judge him;
chunks.st: as the king neither judges others nor do others judge him;

chunks.en: he does not act as a witness, and others are not witnesses about him.
chunks.st: he does not testify nor do others testify against him.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, a demand that he testify is not applicable.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists which korban each person brings for a sin done by mistake: a regular person, the king, the Kohen Gadol and the beis din. For avodah zarah the korbanos are different.

chunks.en: For all the mitzvos in the Torah that one is punished for
chunks.st: For all mitzvot that are in the Torah for whose intentional

chunks.en: with kares if done on purpose, and needs a chatas if done by mistake,
chunks.st: violation one is liable to receive karet and for whose unwitting violation one is liable to bring a sin-offering,

words.note: A punishment from Hashem of being cut off.
A korban brought for a sin done by mistake.

chunks.en: a regular person brings a female lamb or a female goat,
chunks.st: the individual brings a ewe or female goat for their unwitting transgression,

chunks.en: and the king brings a male goat,
chunks.st: and the king brings a male goat for their unwitting transgression,

words.note: The Nasi here means the king.

chunks.en: and the anointed Kohen and the beis din bring a bull.
chunks.st: and an anointed priest and a court who issued an erroneous ruling bring a bull.

words.note: The Kohen Gadol.

chunks.en: And for avodah zarah,
chunks.st: And for unwittingly engaging in idol worship,

words.note: Avodah zarah is serving idols.

chunks.en: a regular person, the king and the anointed Kohen bring a female goat,
chunks.st: the individual, and the king, and the anointed priest bring a female goat,

chunks.en: and the beis din brings a bull and a goat:
chunks.st: and the court brings a bull and a goat:

chunks.en: the bull as an olah and the goat as a chatas.
chunks.st: A bull for a burnt-offering and a goat for a sin-offering.

words.note: A korban that is burned completely on the mizbe'ach.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches who brings an asham korban and who brings a special korban whose size depends on how rich a person is.

chunks.en: An asham talui:
chunks.st: With regard to a provisional guilt-offering,

words.note: An asham talui is brought when one is not sure he sinned.

chunks.en: a regular person and the king must bring it,
chunks.st: the individual and the king are liable,

words.note: The Nasi here means the king.

chunks.en: but the anointed Kohen and the beis din are free.
chunks.st: and an anointed priest and a court are exempt.

words.note: The Kohen Gadol.

chunks.en: A sure asham:
chunks.st: With regard to a definite guilt-offering,

words.note: An asham brought for a sin one knows he did.

chunks.en: a regular person, the king and the anointed Kohen must bring it,
chunks.st: the individual, the king, and the anointed priest are liable,

chunks.en: but the beis din is free.
chunks.st: and a court is exempt.

chunks.en: For "hearing the voice," for "saying
chunks.st: For hearing of a voice, i.e., a false oath of testimony, and for a false oath on an utterance

chunks.en: with the lips," and for making the Beis HaMikdash or its korbanos tamei,
chunks.st: of the lips, and for the defiling of the Temple or its sacrificial foods,

chunks.en: the beis din is free,
chunks.st: a court is exempt,

chunks.en: but a regular person, the king and the anointed Kohen must bring a korban.
chunks.st: and the individual, the king, and the anointed priest are liable.

chunks.en: Only, the Kohen Gadol does not bring one
chunks.st: But an anointed High Priest is not liable

chunks.en: for making the Beis HaMikdash or its korbanos tamei.
chunks.st: for the defiling of the Temple or its sacrificial foods;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Shimon.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Shimon.

chunks.en: And what do they bring?
chunks.st: And what offering are they liable to bring?

chunks.en: A korban that goes up and down.
chunks.explain: A rich person brings an animal; a poor person brings birds or flour.
chunks.st: It is a sliding-scale offering based on their financial circumstances, as delineated in the Torah (see Leviticus 5:1–13).

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz calls him Rabbi Elazar; our Hebrew and Bartenura say Rabbi Eliezer.

chunks.en: the king brings a goat.
chunks.st: The king brings a goat.

mishnayos.summary: If the Kohen Gadol or the king sinned and then stepped down from his position, he still brings the same korban he would have brought before.

chunks.en: If the anointed Kohen sinned
chunks.st: In the case of an anointed priest who sinned
chunks.stMore: on the basis of his own erroneous halakhic ruling

words.note: The Kohen Gadol, who was anointed with special oil.

chunks.en: and afterwards stepped down from being the Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: and thereafter moved on from his anointment,
chunks.stMore: e.g., if he was disqualified due to a blemish that befell him before he brought his sin-offering,

chunks.en: and the same for a king who sinned
chunks.st: and likewise in the case of a king [nasi] who sinned

words.note: The Nasi here means the king.

chunks.en: and afterwards stepped down from his greatness,
chunks.st: and thereafter moved on from his prominence
chunks.stMore: before he had brought an offering,

chunks.en: the anointed Kohen brings a bull,
chunks.st: an anointed priest brings a bull
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that he is no longer the High Priest,

chunks.en: and the king brings a goat.
chunks.st: and the king brings a goat,
chunks.stMore: as he would have done during his reign.

mishnayos.summary: If the Kohen Gadol stepped down and then sinned, he still brings a bull. But a king who stepped down and then sinned is like a regular person.

chunks.en: If the anointed Kohen stepped down from being Kohen Gadol
chunks.st: In the case of an anointed priest who moved on from his anointment

words.note: The Kohen Gadol, who was anointed with special oil.

chunks.en: and afterwards sinned,
chunks.st: and thereafter sinned,

chunks.en: and the same for a king who stepped down from his greatness
chunks.st: and likewise the king who moved on from his prominence

words.note: The Nasi here means the king.

chunks.en: and afterwards sinned,
chunks.st: and thereafter sinned,

chunks.en: the anointed Kohen brings a bull,
chunks.st: an anointed priest brings a bull,
chunks.stMore: which he would have brought while he was High Priest,

chunks.en: but the king is like a regular person.
chunks.st: and the status of the king is like that of a commoner [kehedyot].

words.note: Someone who is not a king or Kohen Gadol.

mishnayos.summary: If someone sinned before he became king or Kohen Gadol, he brings the korban of a regular person. The king is called Nasi because only Hashem is above him.

chunks.en: If they sinned before they were appointed,
chunks.st: If a king or High Priest sinned before they were appointed,

chunks.en: and afterwards they were appointed,
chunks.st: and thereafter they were appointed,

chunks.en: they are like regular people.
chunks.st: the status of these people is like that of commoners;
chunks.stMore: they bring the sin-offering of an individual.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.he: אִם נוֹדַע לָהֶם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְמַנּוּ,
chunks.en: if they found out about the sin before they were appointed,
chunks.st: If it became known to them, before they were appointed
chunks.stMore: as king or High Priest, that they had sinned,

chunks.en: they must bring a korban. But if after they were appointed,
chunks.st: they are liable to bring the sin-offering of an individual, but if it became known to them after they were appointed as king or High Priest

words.en: and from when they were appointed

chunks.en: they are free. And who is the Nasi?
chunks.st: they are completely exempt. Who is the nasi?

chunks.en: This is the king,
chunks.st: This is a king,

chunks.en: because it says, "And he does one
chunks.st: as it is stated: “When a nasi sins, and performs any one

chunks.en: of all the mitzvos of Hashem his God,"
chunks.st: of all the mitzvot of the Lord his God that shall not be performed, unwittingly, and he is guilty” (Leviticus 4:22),

chunks.en: a Nasi who has no one over him
chunks.st: referring to one who has only

chunks.en: except Hashem his God.
chunks.st: the Lord his God over him and no other authority. That is only the king.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah explains who the anointed Kohen is, and the few differences between different kinds of Kohen Gadol. In most halachos they are all the same.

chunks.en: And who is the anointed Kohen?
chunks.st: And who is the anointed priest?

words.note: The Kohen Gadol who was anointed.

chunks.en: The one anointed with the special anointing oil,
chunks.st: It is the High Priest who is anointed with the anointing oil,

words.note: Special oil that Moshe made to anoint the Kohanim.

chunks.en: not the one who became Kohen Gadol by wearing the extra clothes.
chunks.explain: Later, the oil was hidden, so the Kohen Gadol began by wearing his special clothes.
chunks.st: not the High Priest consecrated by donning multiple garments,
chunks.stMore: i.e., one who served after the anointing oil had been sequestered, toward the end of the First Temple period.

chunks.he: אֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן הַמָּשׁוּחַ בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה
chunks.en: The only difference between the Kohen anointed with the oil
chunks.st: The difference between a High Priest anointed with the anointing oil

chunks.en: and the one with the extra clothes is the bull
chunks.st: and one consecrated by donning multiple garments unique to the High Priest is only that the latter does not bring the bull

chunks.en: that is brought for all the mitzvos.
chunks.explain: Only the anointed one brings a bull for a mistaken ruling.
chunks.st: that comes for the transgression of any of the mitzvot.

chunks.he: וְאֵין בֵּין כֹּהֵן מְשַׁמֵּשׁ לְכֹהֵן שֶׁעָבַר,
chunks.en: And the only difference between the Kohen Gadol who is serving and one who stepped down
chunks.st: And the difference between a High Priest currently serving in that capacity and a former High Priest who had temporarily filled that position while the High Priest was unfit for service

chunks.he: אֶלָּא פַר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וַעֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה.
chunks.en: is the bull of Yom Kippur and the tenth of an eifah.
chunks.explain: The tenth of an eifah is a flour korban the Kohen Gadol brings every day.
chunks.st: is only with regard to the bull brought by the High Priest on Yom Kippur and the tenth of an ephah meal-offering brought by the High Priest daily.
chunks.stMore: Each of these offerings is brought only by the current High Priest, and not by a former High Priest.

words.note: A measure of flour.

chunks.he: זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין בַּעֲבוֹדַת יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
chunks.en: Both are the same in the avodah of Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: Both this High Priest currently serving and that former High Priest are equal with regard to performing the rest of the Yom Kippur service,

chunks.en: and both are commanded to marry a besulah,
chunks.st: and they are both commanded with regard to marrying a virgin (see Leviticus 21:13),

words.note: A girl who was never married before.

chunks.en: and both may not marry a widow,
chunks.st: and it is prohibited for both to marry a widow (see Leviticus 21:14),

chunks.en: and they do not become tamei for their relatives who passed away,
chunks.st: and they may not render themselves impure with impurity imparted by a corpse even in the event that one of their relatives dies (see Leviticus 21:11),

chunks.en: and they do not let their hair grow long when mourning,
chunks.st: and they may not grow their hair long

chunks.en: and they do not tear their clothes,
chunks.st: and they may not rend their garments as expressions of mourning (see Leviticus 21:10),

chunks.en: and when they pass away, the one who killed by accident goes back home.
chunks.explain: He goes home from the city of refuge where he had to stay.
chunks.st: and when they die they restore the unwitting murderer to his home from the city of refuge (see Numbers 35:25).

words.note: Someone who killed a person by accident.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches how a Kohen Gadol mourns differently from a regular Kohen: how he tears his clothing, and whether he may bring korbanos on the day a close relative passed away.

chunks.en: The Kohen Gadol tears his clothes from below,
chunks.st: A High Priest rends his garments from below when he is in mourning,

chunks.en: and a regular Kohen from above.
chunks.st: and an ordinary priest rends his garments from above like a non-priest.

chunks.he: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מַקְרִיב אוֹנֵן וְלֹא אוֹכֵל,
chunks.en: The Kohen Gadol may bring korbanos as an onen, but may not eat from them.
chunks.explain: An onen is a mourner on the day a close relative passed away.
chunks.st: A High Priest sacrifices offerings as an acute mourner, i.e., on the day of the death of one of his close relatives, but he may not eat from those offerings.

words.note: A mourner on the day a close relative passed away.

chunks.en: But a regular Kohen may not bring korbanos and may not eat.
chunks.st: And an ordinary priest who is an acute mourner neither sacrifices offerings nor eats from those offerings.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches what comes first: something that happens more often comes first, and something holier comes first. So the Kohen Gadol's bull comes before the community's bull.

chunks.en: Whatever happens more often than another
chunks.st: Any mitzva that is more frequent than another mitzva

chunks.en: comes before the other.
chunks.st: precedes that other mitzva
chunks.stMore: if the opportunity to fulfill one of them coincides with an opportunity to fulfill the other.

chunks.en: And whatever is holier than another
chunks.st: And anyone who is more sanctified than another

chunks.en: comes before the other.
chunks.st: precedes that other person.

chunks.en: If the bull of the anointed Kohen and the bull of the community are both waiting,
chunks.st: If the bull of the anointed priest and the bull of the congregation, which are brought for absence of awareness of the matter, are pending,

words.note: The Kohen Gadol.

chunks.en: the bull of the anointed Kohen comes before the bull
chunks.st: the bull of the anointed priest precedes the bull

chunks.en: of the community in all its steps.
chunks.st: of the congregation in all its actions, i.e., its sacrificial rites.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches who we help first, a man or a woman, in different kinds of trouble.

chunks.he: הָאִישׁ קוֹדֵם לָאִשָּׁה לְהַחֲיוֹת וּלְהָשִׁיב אֲבֵדָה.
chunks.en: A man comes before a woman to save his life and to give back a lost thing.
And a woman comes before a man to be given clothing,
and to be freed from captivity.
When both are in danger of being harmed,
the man comes first.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists who comes first by family: a Kohen, a Levi, a Yisrael, and so on. But Torah learning is greater than all of it.

chunks.en: A Kohen comes before a Levi,
a Levi before a Yisrael,
a Yisrael before a mamzer,

words.note: A mamzer is someone whose family line keeps him from marrying into most families.

chunks.en: a mamzer before a Givoni,

words.note: From the Givonim, who joined the Jews in Yehoshua's time.

chunks.en: a Givoni before a ger,

words.note: Someone who was not born Jewish and became Jewish.

chunks.en: and a ger before a freed eved.

words.note: A servant who was set free.

chunks.en: When is this? When they are all equal.
chunks.explain: Equal in how much Torah they know.

chunks.he: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה מַמְזֵר תַּלְמִיד חָכָם
chunks.en: But if a mamzer is a talmid chacham,

words.note: A talmid chacham is a Torah scholar.

chunks.en: and a Kohen Gadol knows no Torah,

words.note: An am ha'aretz is someone who has not learned Torah.

chunks.en: the mamzer who is a talmid chacham comes before
the Kohen Gadol who knows no Torah.
